title: Enterprise AI Governance six-layer control register
description: Machine-readable control map for the six enterprise governance layers: Policy; Roles & Accountability; Risk Management; Data & Model Governance; Monitoring & Controls; Audit & Assurance. It is a crosswalk over existing Hawkeye Sterling sources of truth, not a replacement for the AIMS risk register, third-party register, assurance matrix, policy register or AI asset register.
framework_note: The taxonomy was inspired by a six-layer enterprise AI governance practitioner graphic supplied during design review. The repository wording, control mapping and diagram are original; no third-party artwork is stored.

register_review.cadence: Quarterly, and on any new AI asset, provider, model family, material prompt charter, tool/connector, or data-flow change.
register_review.approval_note: Compilation and CI validation do not constitute MLRO, Board, legal or external-auditor approval. Human approvals remain recorded in their authoritative governance documents.

status_semantics.effective: Control is implemented and the named repository evidence exists. This label does not imply external certification.
status_semantics.partial: Control exists, but an identified human, contractual, operational or assurance step remains open.
status_semantics.open: Control objective is applicable but the named assurance activity has not yet been completed.
status_semantics.not_applicable: Control objective is not applicable to the current system boundary; rationale must be recorded.

layers.name: Policy
layers.purpose: Define principles, permitted use, approval gates and regulatory alignment.

layers.name: Roles & Accountability
layers.purpose: Assign accountable owners, decision rights, legal oversight and escalation.

layers.name: Risk Management
layers.purpose: Identify, classify, assess, mitigate and explicitly treat residual AI risk.

layers.name: Data & Model Governance
layers.purpose: Govern data, prompts, models, providers, lineage, versions, access and retention.

layers.name: Monitoring & Controls
layers.purpose: Monitor performance, bias, drift, security, incidents and continuous control operation.

layers.name: Audit & Assurance
layers.purpose: Preserve evidence, test controls, audit governance, track remediation and support independent assurance.

controls.name: AI principles and policy
controls.note: Defines the governing AI principles and maps them to the UAE AI Charter.

controls.name: Acceptable-use rules
controls.note: Permitted and prohibited use is documented and the Advisor has an acknowledgment gate.

controls.name: AI use-case approval criteria
controls.cadence: Per new or materially changed AI use case
controls.note: A repository intake gate is implemented in this change; formal organizational adoption remains a human governance act.

controls.name: Regulatory and framework alignment
controls.cadence: At least annual and on material legal change
controls.note: Self-assessment crosswalks are maintained; external certification is not implied.

controls.name: Named accountable owner for every AI asset
controls.note: Every registered AI surface carries ownership, risk tier and oversight posture.

controls.name: Business ownership and operating RACI
controls.note: Separates accountability, operation, review and escalation responsibilities.

controls.name: AI governance committee and legal oversight
controls.cadence: Quarterly and on material governance decision
controls.note: The charter exists, while the repository's open-actions register still records human ratification actions.

controls.name: Escalation paths and human decision authority
controls.note: AI remains advisory; escalation and override authority remain human.

controls.name: AI risk identification and scoring
controls.note: AI risks are scored on inherent and residual likelihood-impact positions.

controls.name: Risk appetite and residual-risk treatment
controls.note: The repository currently reports risks above appetite and does not infer acceptance without a human decision.

controls.name: Impact and privacy assessment
controls.cadence: On new use case, new data flow, new provider and material change
controls.note: Privacy and stakeholder impacts are assessed separately from model performance.

controls.name: Mitigation and corrective-action tracking
controls.note: Findings are routed to CAPA/open actions with closure evidence.

controls.name: Use-case classification before deployment
controls.cadence: Per new or materially changed AI use case
controls.note: The intake form requires classification and risk tiering; organizational ratification of the new gate remains explicit.

controls.name: AI inventory and system boundary
controls.note: Shadow-AI drift is checked against model API callers.

controls.name: Data lineage, minimisation and retention
controls.note: Inputs, retention and cross-border considerations are documented.

controls.name: Prompt and model version/change control
controls.note: Prompt fingerprints and model routing changes are CI-governed.

controls.name: Model validation and bias evaluation
controls.cadence: Weekly live evaluation; quarterly bias review; on model change
controls.note: Validation covers governed use of external models rather than claiming validation of the provider's foundation model.

controls.name: AI and AI-adjacent vendor assurance
controls.cadence: At onboarding, annually, and on material provider change
controls.note: The live GRC metric reports outstanding third-party assurance items; gated features remain gated where required.

controls.name: Tool, connector and access governance
controls.note: Capabilities, credentials and agent authorization are explicitly inventoried.

controls.name: AI performance and behavioural monitoring
controls.note: Offline and live evals provide repeatable behavioural assurance.

controls.name: Bias and drift monitoring
controls.cadence: Quarterly bias review; continuous configuration drift checks
controls.note: Bias testing and governance-drift counters are separate controls.

controls.name: Security and access controls
controls.cadence: Per build and continuous runtime configuration
controls.note: Application and repository security controls are tested independently of model quality.

controls.name: Incident detection, response and control freshness
controls.cadence: Daily freshness; incident-driven response; annual exercise
controls.note: Detection and response are implemented; the AI risk register records the first tabletop exercise as an outstanding mitigation.

controls.name: Governance metrics and continuous reporting
controls.note: Metrics are computed from repository evidence and drift-checked in CI.

controls.name: Control-to-evidence assurance map
controls.note: Automated proof paths are checked for existence and reflected in the control-effectiveness metric.

controls.name: Internal audit programme
controls.note: The programme exists; the open-actions register records the first thematic review as a human action still to complete.

controls.name: Management review and governance decisions
controls.note: Templates and decision rights exist; this register does not fabricate completed meetings or approvals.

controls.name: Preservation of decisions and audit evidence
controls.note: Decision provenance, audit trails and evidence retention are part of the assurance matrix.

controls.name: Remediation tracking and closure
controls.note: CAPA closure is measured as a management metric rather than asserted.

controls.name: Independent external assurance
controls.note: No third-party AI governance or ISO 42001 conformity audit is claimed. The repository remains a self-assessed control environment unless and until an external review is commissioned.
